question: What finally ended the Dutch monopoly on nutmeg and cloves, which rival navies had failed to break?
answer: Smuggled seedlings. Around 1770, expeditions sent by Pierre Poivre, the French administrator of Mauritius, brought living clove and nutmeg plants out of the Dutch-held Moluccas. Planted on Mauritius and later in other colonies, they spread across the tropics. Grenada, in the Caribbean, now carries a nutmeg on its national flag.
move: A monopoly built on where something grows ends when it can be moved.
